column1: # Reverse with k3 KL to the anchor on every replayed token (common.repair --kl_beta), no
# floor, no down-weight, no retain term, on the four pilot anchors: lr 1e-6, fresh AdamW,
# 8 warm-up updates, 16 groups an update, 256 updates; every listed dose kept as a weight
# diff, doses 32/64/128/256 evaluated (with token drift) while the replay runs.
# beta 0.025 and 0.1 in both environments: median |A| is 0.50 on multihop and 0.12 on
# creatures, so creatures at 0.025 and multihop at 0.1 match in |A|/beta (soft floor
# log(1 + |A|/beta) = 1.8 nats) while the other pairs match in beta itself.
# On Tidewater, one chain per B200 (its evals stream into a persistent engine), one job
# per line. Throughput A/B, paired by run: beta 0.025 at the defaults, beta 0.1 with
# creatures micro-batch 8 (MICRO_BATCH applies to creatures lines only; multihop keeps 2):
#   LINES=4 KL_BETA=0.025 ARM_TAG=revkl025 FLOOR= OPTIM_DEVICE=cuda MH_MICRO_BATCH=2 \
#   EVAL_DOSES=32,64,128,256 sbatch -A humanpref-igor --time=5:00:00 \
#     --gpus-per-node=b200:1 --cpus-per-task=14 --mem=257G --chdir=$URH_ROOT \
#     --output=$URH_OUT/reverse-%j.out sycophancy/jobs/reverse_batch.sh \
#     sycophancy/jobs/plans/reverse_kl.tsv
#   (beta 0.1: KL_BETA=0.1 ARM_TAG=revkl100 MICRO_BATCH=8)
# Both held the hack (docs/LOG.md 2026-11-25), and a k3 cap of 10 nats let single flipped
# tokens take whole updates. Second batch, cap 5 (common.repair's default since), a
# quarter of the beta that matched in |A|/beta (|A|/beta 20): multihop 0.025 (lines 1, 2:
# against the cap-10 arm, the cap's effect) and creatures 0.00625 (lines 3, 4):
#   LINES=1 KL_BETA=0.025 ARM_TAG=revkl025c5 ... (likewise LINES=2)
#   LINES=3 KL_BETA=0.00625 ARM_TAG=revkl006c5 MICRO_BATCH=8 ... (likewise LINES=4)
